messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] high error rate detected in us-west-2 on continuous-batcher. 30% 5xx on /v1/chat/completions, latency > 10s. Pager -> @maya @ashwin @jordan-sre

maya: acked. I'm seeing batcher pool 'cb-west' queue depth climbing across nodes cb-west-3/4/7. Noticed repeated container restarts on cb-west-4. grabbing logs now.

maya: log excerpt:
maya: ```
[2025-08-03T20:58:32Z] runtime: cuda driver error: out of memory allocating 900 MiB
[2025-08-03T20:58:33Z] kubelet: container "continuous-batcher" oomkilled (exit 137)
[2025-08-03T20:58:33Z] batcher: shard reassign triggered
```

ashwin: any recent infra changes?

maya: yes, a runtime kernel tweak and driver bump to nvidia-driver 525.60 rolled to us-west-2 at ~20:45.

jordan-sre: adding kernel logs: saw elevated page-faults and DMA mapping errors on cb-west-4. Looks like significant swap activity -> heavy page-in -> OOM cycles. Paging thrash seems likely.

lydia-ops: customer impact: two enterprise tenants reported timeouts. Preparing status update; will wait for mitigation details.

maya: mitigation step 1: temporarily disable dynamic batching and set BATCHER_MAX_QUEUE=200 to keep queue bounded. Patch sent to cluster for the affected deployment. Command used:
maya: ```bash
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/continuous-batcher DYNAMIC_BATCHING=off BATCHER_MAX_QUEUE=200
```

ashwin: good call. I'm also changing routing for critical production routes to fallback to cpu-optimized model (open-redwood-cpu-small) to reduce GPU pressure. Doing via control-plane API.

ashwin: curl -s -X POST https://cp.internal/api/routes/fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"open-redwood-cpu-small","priority":100}'

maya: after env change and fallback, observed error rate drop to ~9% and p95 latency reduced from 17s -> 2.4s on fallback paths. cb-west-4 still flapped once during restart loop.

jordan-sre: suggestion: cordon the worst nodes to prevent noisy neighbor effects. kubectl cordon cb-west-4 && kubectl drain cb-west-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

maya: cordoned cb-west-4. drain started; some long-tail requests timed out — we replayed a handful to CPU pool. No data loss.

eng-runtime: triage note: fused attention path in the runtime uses a new temporary buffer reuse optimization introduced in last runtime patch; reproduce locally shows incorrect accounting on certain cuda kernels causing underflow in free list. Candidate fix: add explicit buffer fence and sanity check counters.

ashwin: plan: test runtime patch with synthetic heavy-batching workload in staging (same driver + kernel version). If reproduces, prepare hotfix and rollback plan for us-west-2.

lydia-ops: status page draft: "Investigating elevated errors and latency for inference requests in us-west-2. Traffic for critical routes temporarily routed to CPU variants. Engineers are working on mitigating GPU memory thrash. Updates every 20–30 minutes." Publish?

maya: publish now. Also create incident ticket INC-2025-4822 and attach logs and dmesg.

incident-bot: [ACTION] Handoff requested: maya -> ashwin for ongoing triage and communication. Handoff ETA 10m.

maya: handing off to @ashwin. Leaving notes in the ticket, collecting core dumps and nv-host-status.

ashwin: taking over. Current metrics: error-rate 5.1%, overall latency ~1.9s on fallback routes, GPUs still report high memory pressure but no widespread restarts after cordon/fallback. Next: reproduce and validate runtime fix. If we can't reproduce, plan B is rollback driver to previous stable 520.xx.

jordan-sre: continuing to monitor host flaps. kernel dmesg shows repeated GPU page faults at addresses in tensor buffers; likely triggered by the new kernel-level DMA mapping change. SRE recommends keeping affected nodes cordoned until hotfix verified.

ashwin: cordoned list updated: cb-west-4, cb-west-7. rolling restart only on non-affected nodes to pick up batching limit env.

lydia-ops: sent targeted emails to impacted accounts; one customer asked for credit and timeline—escalating to customer success.

eng-runtime: patch landed to a branch. Quick test in staging with stress harness shows reduced memory accounting mismatches. We'll run longer 30m soak with heavy sequence lengths to validate.

ashwin: good. If green, we'll roll hotfix to us-west-2 as a canary on a single node pool, monitor for 15m, then rollout. If not, rollback driver to 520.45 as fallback.

maya: additional note: collected /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and coredumps uploaded to ticket. Leaving for ashwin.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] last_alert: 1918681300. Current error-rate: 3.8%. Next scheduled update in 30m.

ashwin: patch applied to canary nodes; early signals look good (no new OOMs on canary). Proceeding with staged rollout. Will update when canary reaches 15m stable.

lydia-ops: keeping status page live and will post update after canary 15m.

maya: thanks all. I'll sync into postmortem once hotfix is confirmed. Great cross-team coordination :thumbsup:
